thread:
Mira: Quick heads-up — profiler shows a pattern causing OOMs during batch formation when we eagerly include requests with large KV footprints. Happened 3x in last hour (p99 latency spike + OOM on c4-prod).
Devin: Can you paste the relevant stack/profile?
Mira: Sure, pasted below. It's the batch admission stage where we compute 'batch_token_budget' then naively accept queued reqs until budget exhausted. Problem: we use token-only budget, not kv_size.
Mira: ```
BatchAdmission::form_batch()
  budget = calc_token_budget(queue)
  for r in queue:
    if r.tokens <= budget:
      include(r)
      budget -= r.tokens
    else: break
```
Mira: Example: 1 small req (512 tokens, kv=1.2MB) + 6 medium reqs (256 tokens each, kv=3.4MB each) -> tokens under budget, but kv pushes mem over threshold.
Ashley: So token-first admission is insufficient. We need a combined metric or predicate. Maybe prefilter by estimated_kv and apply a soft cap on per-batch-kv.
Devin: Agreed. Proposal: compute batch_kv_est = sum(est_kv) and reject any candidate that would push batch_kv_est > kv_soft_limit. Keep token budget as secondary ordering heuristic.
Ryan: How do we estimate est_kv reliably? We already have a histogram keyed by model+prefix_len; it's noisy but good enough. Use percentile (p90) per key to be conservative.
Mira: I ran a quick sim with p90 estimates and a soft_limit=0.8*mem_watermark and it eliminated the OOMs in the trace. But it increased tail latency for tiny requests because we ended up denying batching so they went to single-request execution more often.
Ashley: Can we add a priority rule: if a request is tiny tokens and kv_est small, allow it to bypass kv check (to avoid hurting tiny requests). Also allow the batcher to do one speculative eviction: if a new candidate would exceed soft_limit but total token value is high, try a single best-effort eviction of the oldest low-priority entry.
Devin: Eviction during formation is tricky — we do partial KV evict that invalidates prefixes. Risky for cached continuations. But we could implement transient 'soft-evict' that doesn't persist to global cache: a form of temporary spare memory allocation for batch assembly. Implementation complexity high.
bench-bot: PERF: sim_run=2026-03-15T09:02Z; config=kv_p90_filter,soft_limit=0.8; result: OOM_count=0, tail_latency_p99=+9.8% for tiny-reqs, avg_cost -3.1%.
Mira: Those numbers match my local run. Tradeoff look real. Next idea: hybrid admission order — sort queue by kv_density = est_kv / tokens and prefer low kv_density first, subject to token budget. That reduces batch_kv while keeping throughput.
Ryan: Kernel selection interaction: if we push high-kv requests to single-host execution we may want to switch to a more memory-friendly kernel (slower) to avoid OOM. We should tag requests with 'kv_hot' to pick kernels at runtime.
Ashley: Good call. Add request attribute 'kv_hot' if est_kv > per-request_threshold; admission will avoid batching kv_hot unless batch_kv_est remains low. If admitted, runtime picks kv-friendly kernel path.
Devin: We should also export metrics: batch_kv_est, kv_rejected_count, kv_evicted_count, and kv_density_hist. That will help tune soft_limit and thresholds.
Mira: I'll prototype: 1) p90 est_kv lookup, 2) kv_soft_limit = 0.75*mem_watermark, 3) ordering by kv_density then tokens, 4) allow tiny bypass, 5) emit metrics. Will run sim and canaries.
Ashley: Can we add a small canary in prod that gates on node-level memory headroom so we don't globally flip? Use per-GPU headroom check before admitting.
Devin: Yes. Batcher should check node_headroom > margin before allowing any batch_kv_est growth over soft_limit. That prevents wide blast radius.
Mira: Kicking off branch now. Will post a short PR and bench results.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: branch=mira/eager-kv-filter, target=canary-prod, reviewers=@Devin,@Ashley
Ryan: Thanks — let's keep the rollout slow and watch kv_rejected_count and p99 latency.
Mira: Will do. I'll update in this thread with the perf graphs and config knobs. :eyes:
